title: The right to act, never to the fruit
hookLine: the most quoted line in the Gita, the one on posters and in commencement speeches, and what it actually says
carry: the doing is yours, the fruit isn't

lines: ON A POSTER, A MUG, A SPEECH.
cards: You've probably met this verse without knowing it. On a poster in a yoga studio, in a graduation speech, on a mug: do your work, and don't worry about the results. It sounds like a nice bit of stress advice.
It's stranger, and more demanding. It comes in the middle of Krishna's second chapter, just after he tells Arjuna, now I'll teach you a different way of seeing.
And a man on a battlefield needed it more than anyone with a mug.

teach.b: Krishna starts with a promise. In this path, he says, no effort is ever lost, and even a little of it protects you from great fear.

Then he warns about a certain kind of religion, full of flowery words and rituals performed to get rewards. Then the line itself, chapter two, verse forty-seven. In Sanskrit: karmany evadhikaras te, ma phaleshu kadachana.

teach.h: YOUR RIGHT IS TO THE ACTION ALONE.
teach.b: Your right is to the action alone, never to its fruits. And he keeps going, which the posters usually don't. Ma karma phala hetur bhur: don't let the fruit be your motive.

teach.h: NOT ATTACHED TO NOT ACTING EITHER.
teach.b: Ma te sango 'stv akarmani: and don't be attached to not acting, either. Krishna isn't saying care less. You get the doing; the results were never yours to own.

Plant the tree, water the tree, protect the tree. Whether it fruits, and who eats the fruit, belongs to something larger. And Arjuna can't use that as a reason to sit down, because not acting is just another attachment.
Then Krishna gives it a name. Samatvam yoga uchyate. Evenness is called yoga: steady in success, steady in failure.
Two verses later, a second well-known definition: yogah karmasu kaushalam.

teach.h: EVENNESS IS YOGA. SKILL IN ACTION.
THE DOING IS YOURS. THE FRUIT ISN'T.
teach.b: So yoga, in the Gita, isn't first a posture. It's a way of working: fully, well, and without clutching. For Arjuna, frozen because of what the fight will cost, this is the first way out.
He doesn't have to control how it ends. He has to do what's his, well, with his hands open. Hindu teachers call this nishkama karma: action without craving its fruit.

how: Gita 2.47, karmany evadhikaras te, is one of the most memorized verses in Hindu life; many Hindus recite it before work or exams, and 2.48 and 2.50 are often quoted as the Gita's definitions of yoga.

o: a duty a king lays on you
your right, what is yours to claim
the reward you earn for good work

games.q: what's inside the line — tap the pairs.
p: your right is to the action alone

s: the verse says to stop caring about your work
it says the doing is yours, fully. only the fruit isn't.
the verse also warns against being attached to not acting
ma te sango 'stv akarmani: don't cling to inaction either.
in the Gita, yoga first means a posture
it's called evenness, and skill in action: a way of working.

games.q: you're Arjuna. you've just heard your right is to action, never to its fruit. so the result isn't yours. what follows?
o: then I don't have to act at all.
then I act fully, and let go of the result.
then I act only when I'm sure it'll work.
games.why: act fully, and let the result go. Krishna closes the loophole: don't be attached to not acting, either.

practice: Rest your hands on your knees, palms up, and think of something you're working hard on, and how badly you want it to turn out a certain way.

Keep the work, the next email, the next rehearsal, the next honest conversation, and let go of the outcome. Many Hindus say this verse before an exam or a day's work; if you like, say it once, softly: karmany evadhikaras te.
Each time you breathe out, let your palms soften a little more.

wordCard.voice: Adhikara. Your right. Karmany evadhikaras te: your right is to the action alone, never to its fruits.

orig.note: Sanskrit, Gita 2.47: your right is to action alone. karma, action; adhikara, right.

carryVoice: Your line: the doing is yours, the fruit isn't. Karmany evadhikaras te. Until tomorrow.

sources.q: karmany evadhikaras te, ma phaleshu kadachana
